sources.name: CISA Advisories
sources.bias_note: US government body; authoritative on US-facing threats, careful wording, rarely attributes publicly, slow on non-US incidents.

sources.name: CISA News
sources.bias_note: Agency press office; frames events around its own programs and successes.

sources.name: CyberScoop
sources.bias_note: Washington-focused trade outlet; strong on policy and federal sourcing, sponsor-funded events with vendors.

sources.name: The Record (Recorded Future News)
sources.bias_note: Editorially independent but owned by threat-intel vendor Recorded Future; strong on nation-state and ransomware actors.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.bias_note: Fast, incident-driven, often first with ransomware claims; headlines can run ahead of confirmation.

sources.name: SecurityWeek
sources.bias_note: Vendor-advertising supported; dedicated ICS/OT coverage, sometimes echoes vendor research uncritically.

sources.name: Dark Reading
sources.bias_note: Informa-owned, heavy vendor sponsorship; analysis-led, can amplify vendor threat reports.

sources.name: Krebs on Security
sources.bias_note: Single investigative reporter; deep on cybercrime ecosystems, selective coverage, US-centric.

sources.name: Utility Dive
sources.bias_note: Utility-industry trade outlet; frames security through regulation, cost and reliability; sympathetic to utilities.

sources.name: DOE Newsroom
sources.bias_note: Department press releases; promotional about federal programs.

sources.name: UK NCSC News
sources.bias_note: UK government agency; aligned with Five Eyes attributions.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.bias_note: High volume, sponsored content mixed with news; good for the wide-angle view of what else is happening.

sources.name: Industrial Cyber
sources.bias_note: ICS/OT-only trade outlet; vendor-advertising supported, relays vendor reports and regulator notices with little pushback.

sources.name: The Register Security
sources.bias_note: Irreverent UK tech press; sceptical of vendors and governments alike, headline tone can trivialise.

sources.name: arXiv cs.CR (preprints)
sources.bias_note: Unreviewed preprints; author claims, not findings; good for what researchers are probing (ICS intrusion detection, grid attacks) before journals publish.

sources.name: arXiv eess.SY (systems and control preprints)
sources.bias_note: Control-systems research, including grid and cyber-physical security; unreviewed.

sources.name: Schneier on Security
sources.bias_note: One academic's commentary and links; strong on policy and crypto, selective, opinionated.

sources.name: CSIS
sources.bias_note: Washington think tank; policy analysis with funders across defence and industry; frames through US strategic interest.

sources.name: Kaspersky ICS CERT
sources.bias_note: Deep ICS vulnerability and threat research from a Russian vendor banned from US federal use (2017) and US sales (2024); technical content is strong, attribution of Russian activity is absent or soft.

sources.name: WIRED Security
sources.bias_note: Narrative long-form; strong investigative pieces on Sandworm and grid attacks; prioritises story over timeliness; Condé Nast.
